summary: node1 now runs the worker persistently as inventory-worker with kernel-enforced limits of 25% of one CPU and 128 MiB. The service recovered successfully after a verified node reboot.
actions_performed: Created the locked inventory-worker system account.
Created and enabled a supervised OpenRC service for the worker.
Rebooted node1 safely and verified its changed boot identity and full service recovery.

evidence.summary: The worker process has UID 103 and GID 104, mapped to inventory-worker, with the expected executable command line.

evidence.requirement: CPU limited to at most 25% of one CPU
evidence.summary: The live service cgroup reports cpu.max=25000 100000. A post-restart saturated 10-second sample averaged 25.0% and recorded throttling in every period.
The live service cgroup reports memory.max=134217728 bytes; post-restart usage was approximately 1.01 MiB.

Healthy baseline boot ID a1a38abb-fc4f-495e-b5e8-5e1715c788aa was captured, reboot acknowledged, and the new boot ID 07ad3d68-18fb-4d99-a91d-21ed1754bd6f proved restart. Both cgroups and inventory-worker recovered, the executable checksum matched, limits remained active, and the worker stayed alive under load.
